title: occupancy-hedged-queue-manager-and-fleet-throttle-shim
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Dedicated pools need a way to honor per-tenant throughput guarantees while absorbing transient demand spikes without violating latency SLOs or starving other tenants. Current admission uses simple token buckets and per-request reject thresholds which either over-shed or let queues grow and blow tail latency.

Goal: Implement an "occupancy-hedged" queue manager paired with a lightweight fleet throttle shim that: 1) estimates real-time GPU occupancy and headroom, 2) exposes soft per-tenant admission windows that hedge against immediate overload, 3) integrates autoscaler hints (occupancy trends) to avoid cascading falls, and 4) provides graceful degradation (spill to best-effort lane, fallback model variant, or controlled reject) when sustained capacity pressure is detected.

Scope: design and implement control plane + runtime admission hook for Dedicated runtime. Deliverables include design doc, phase-1 prototype (queue manager + shim), unit/integration tests, metrics/dashboards, and a canary rollout plan.

Non-goals: full rewrite of autoscaler; complex market-based allocation; tenant billing changes.

Key ideas: occupancy estimation (GPU busy fraction + KV cache pressure), hedging window (short time buffer to allow bursts that fit current headroom), adjustable soft caps (rate tokens consumed with backoff penalty), progressive fallback (best-effort lane -> lower-qps variant -> reject), autoscaler hinting (expose occupancy percentiles and trend features), and safety net (global emergency shedder with low-latency operator override).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Runtime and Autoscaler leads
Prototype deployed to staging handling synthetic burst tests without tail latency >2x baseline
Metrics show <1% incorrect rejection under mixed workloads and per-tenant throughput guarantees honored within 5% over 5m windows
Canary run plan documented with rollback and operator controls
comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after postmortem of 2026-03-08 incident where a sudden cross-tenant burst led to 3x p99 for a critical customer. Initial notes attached in proposal_links.

2026-03-11 | Luca Martinez: Spike experiment in staging shows GPU occupancy metric (avg busy fraction) correlates with onset of tail latency. Started prototype for occupancy estimator using per-device scheduler timers.

2026-03-11 | Priya Desai (Runtime): Reviewed approach. Concern: hedging window must account for KV cache pressure; otherwise evictions cause large latency spikes. Suggest adding 'cache pressure' penalty to occupancy score.

2026-03-12 | Luca Martinez: Integrated cache pressure metric (cache_eviction_rate per second normalized) into estimator. Benchmarks: median latency steady, p95 improved vs token-bucket-only baseline under 20% extra load.
2026-03-12 | SRE: Request adding emergency-shedder operator API and dashboard widget to allow on-call to toggle global soft caps during capacity incidents.
2026-03-12 | Aisha Kapoor: Updated acceptance criteria to include operator controls and canary plan. Adding dependency to ENG-531004 for fleet-level fallback routing.

2026-03-12 | Luca Martinez: Plan for phase-1 rollout: staging -> internal canary (10% dedicated traffic) -> customer canary (select tenants) with observability gating (latency, correct_rejects, missrate).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive hedging reduces immediate rejects but may delay autoscaler response. To mitigate, we will emit occupancy trends as autoscaler hints and keep hedging window short (200-500ms).
Alternative explored: purely predictive admission using short-term ML model. Rejected for phase-1 due to complexity and maintenance cost.
Operator UX: provide slider for hedging aggressiveness and emergency shed thresholds in Console.
